  - property at risk: *Decidable AND proof-free in the SAFE FRAGMENT (ordinary code), ordinary code composes seam primitives WITHOUT itself crossing the seam (concentration + sound re-import), ownership derived from the proof layer*
  - surfaced by: The SEAM construct — give the formal syntax and typing of the seam: how ordinary (safe) code enters proof-land, what machine-checked obligation it discharges there, and how it re-exports a CHECKED SAFE INTERFACE that ordinary code then uses WITHOUT itself crossing the seam. Give formation / introduction / elimination rules.
  - Decidable proof-free safe code can't soundly use capabilities whose safety is a separation invariant — The seam exists to hand ordinary code capabilities (unique Held tokens, owned bytes, invariant-bearing atomics) over the very primitives whose safety is a concurrent-separation-logic resource invariant with ghost state — provably not a decidable Val×Heap→Prop/SMT goal (RustBelt/Iris). A capability is sound only where its invariant is enforced at the point of use, but a proof-free decidable fragment can enforce linearity, not resource invariants. So the invariant has nowhere safe to live: drop it and the token aliases (existential laundering R0, nested-open double tokens R1, cross-seam reinterpretation under contradictory R R2, ghost-to-memory minting R3 — every soundness kill), or re-thread it linearly and ordinary code is back across the seam (ATS2 cliff, 'worse than pre-borrow Rust', exclusivity wall blocking shared atomics — every ergonomics kill). Sound re-import is the property that mechanically gives.
- **[HARD] Decidable AND proof-free in the SAFE FRAGMENT ✕ Ownership without GC, derived from the proof layer**  <sub>(within failed question)</sub>
  - property at risk: *Decidable AND proof-free in the SAFE FRAGMENT, Ownership without GC, derived from the proof layer, Seam concentration (ordinary code composes primitives WITHOUT crossing the seam)*
  - surfaced by: The SAFE FRAGMENT — the decidable, proof-free, GC-free ownership discipline for ordinary single-threaded code that needs NO seam and NO SMT, derived from the proof layer. State it precisely (move/borrow/lifetime rules).
  - Proof-free decidable safe checking cannot soundly resolve aliasing through reborrow/deref chains — Whether a reborrow taken through a pointer (`&mut *r1`, `&mut **rr`, `&(**rr)[0]`) creates a second live `&mut`, or outlives its supporting loan, is a SEMANTIC provenance fact about runtime aliasing through pointers — invisible to any syntactic rule and to fixed outlives/liveness propagation, the only devices a proof-free, SMT-free, decidable checker may use. Every revision proved this: under-constrain the deref and you accept two live `&mut`/use-after-free (R0–R3); over-constrain to recover soundness and you either falsify uniqueness-over-in-scope-loans (R1's ★) or reject ordinary unsafe-free code the design forbids rejecting (`v.push(v.len())`, `get_default`, the NLL→Polonius gap, R2). The fact that lands precisely between is exactly a per-crossing disjointness/provenance obligation — a SEAM obligation — but it is generated pervasively by ordinary deref-chain code, so discharging it soundly forces ordinary code across the seam (violating concentration), while excluding it leaves the safe fragment unsound or over-restrictive.
- **[HARD] Decidable AND proof-free in the SAFE FRAGMENT (ordinary code) ✕ Sound re-import (no unsound obligation laundering UB into safe code)**  <sub>(within failed question)</sub>
  - property at risk: *Decidable AND proof-free in the SAFE FRAGMENT (ordinary code), Sound re-import (no unsound obligation laundering UB into safe code), Seam CONCENTRATION (ordinary code composes foundations without crossing the seam)*
  - surfaced by: BEHIND THE SEAM — concretely, what obligation does a foundation author discharge, in-language, to implement (a) a lock-free SPSC queue, (b) an MMIO read-to-clear register, (c) an intrusive doubly-linked list — and how does each re-export a safe interface the safe fragment can use without proofs?
  - Decidable proof-free composition cannot soundly re-export shared, aliased, or thread-affine foundations — The cheap, decidable safe fragment is necessarily structural (affine ownership / points-to footprints / structural Send-gates), which is sound only for separated, owned, sequential resources. But the foundations the seam exists to vend — lock-free queues, thread-affine guards, intrusive lists, DMA/MMIO — are exactly the non-separated ones, whose soundness depends on semantic invariants (shared invariants, core affinity, Send-closedness, borrow expiry, shape invariants, relaxed-memory order) that no decidable structural check can observe. So the gap must be paid: either the structural composition rule bridges it unsoundly and launders UB (J∗J⊢False, Send minted for IrqGuard, Container<T> skipping Send T, circular footprints, trusted DMA assertions), or composition must carry the real per-structure proof, which makes every novel foundation a fresh research-grade seam and collapses concentration into the ATS2 cliff. The recurring pattern — `spawn(try_push) ‖ spawn(try_pop)` typechecking affinely while its concurrent image is False — is the canonical exhibit.
- **[HARD] Decidable AND proof-free in the SAFE FRAGMENT (ordinary code) ✕ FIRST-CLASS MACHINE-CHECKED SEAM (sound re-import)**  <sub>(within failed question)</sub>
  - property at risk: *Decidable AND proof-free in the SAFE FRAGMENT (ordinary code), FIRST-CLASS MACHINE-CHECKED SEAM (sound re-import), Seam CONCENTRATION — ordinary code composes seam primitives without crossing the seam*
  - surfaced by: SEAM SOUNDNESS / re-import — the rule that makes crossing BACK sound: how does the safe fragment trust a seam-crossed primitive without re-verifying it, and what structurally stops an unsound obligation from laundering UB into safe code?
  - A seam interface sound enough to re-import is undecidable to compose proof-free — To soundly re-import the chosen primitives (allocators, atomics, lock-free queues, MMIO), the exported interface must carry shared/splittable/persistent, address-pinned, relaxed-memory resources — i.e. separation logic with sharing. But matching held resources against such a primitive's precondition at a use site IS SL frame inference (NP-complete to undecidable for fractions, persistent predicates, and nonlinear `n·size T` indices; Iris-grade interactive proof, not SMT-replayable), so the entailment supposedly confined to seam definitions reappears at every seam use — destroying the decidable, proof-free safe fragment. The only fix that restores decidability — indivisible opaque tokens — cannot express the shared-state concurrency those very primitives require (the multi-producer queue / Arc pattern), so seam concentration collapses: composing the primitives becomes a crossing. Decidable-proof-free and sound-expressive-re-import pull the interface in opposite directions, and seam concentration is what mechanically breaks.
- **[HARD] Decidable AND proof-free in the SAFE FRAGMENT ✕ Seam concentration with sound re-import (ordinary code composes seams without crossing)**  <sub>(within failed question)</sub>
  - property at risk: *Decidable AND proof-free in the SAFE FRAGMENT, Seam concentration with sound re-import (ordinary code composes seams without crossing), Ownership without GC, derived from the proof layer — holds in the safe fragment*
  - surfaced by: SEAM CONCENTRATION & ergonomics — the language mechanism and the argument that keep ordinary code from ever crossing the seam (the checked-interface boundary), and why the obligation stays with a handful of foundation authors. Exhibit a realistic program where ~99% of code is seam-free.
  - Proof-free decidable safe code cannot state the cross-seam relations sound composition needs — A safe fragment made decidable-and-proof-free has no relational vocabulary, so cross-seam side conditions — inter-seam region disjointness, physical aliasing under translation, Send/Sync of captured auxiliary state — are unstateable; therefore two individually-sound seams pointed at one shared resource compose into a data race in zero-obligation depth-0 code, and no obligation fires because none can be expressed. The recurring exhibit is identical each revision: two sound seams sharing an address/refcount/Cell/bit-band word race while the type system reports clean (ADC+ring, Rc::clone+spawn, &Cell capture, bit-band). The only repair — enrich the exterior to state and check the relation — reintroduces exactly what Property 4 forbids: QF-LIA-plus-separation-algebra / nonlinear / higher-order separation-logic obligations that are SMT-or-undecidable, and constructs the closed exterior cannot abstract, pushing obligations into ordinary code (the ATS2 cliff) and destroying both concentration and the 99%-seam-free claim.
- **[HARD] Zero-cost — all proofs, including seam obligations, erase at compile time ✕ Sound re-import — crossing back from a seam must restore the safe fragment's invariants with no laundered UB**  <sub>(within failed question)</sub>
  - property at risk: *Zero-cost — all proofs, including seam obligations, erase at compile time, Sound re-import — crossing back from a seam must restore the safe fragment's invariants with no laundered UB, Seam concentration in foundational effectful primitives (allocators, atomics, MMIO, lock-free)*
  - surfaced by: ZERO-COST SEAM ERASURE — how every seam obligation/witness erases at compile time with a formal guarantee it leaves no runtime trace.
  - Erasing seam witnesses to reach zero-cost also erases the effects they gate — Zero-cost is delivered by erasure, a syntactic relevance/multiplicity judgment that deletes any grade-0 term and claims grade-0 implies no runtime trace. But seam concentration forces the effectful primitives (writes, atomics, MMIO) to live AT the seam, fused to the very proof witnesses that authorize them, so the term that must erase (the witness) and the term that must not (the effect) are one object. Every revision exhibits the same accepted program — `let x:^0 = store r v in body`, `box(close y):♯Unit`, `f(seal(r,()))` — where an erasable-graded seam term still fires a physical store or consumes an owned handle, and ⌊·⌋ silently drops it; pinning the primitive's operands at ω never helps because the effect rides out on the unpinned sequencing/bind combinator. No relevance lattice can separate 'proof, delete it' from 'fires a store, keep it' when the proof's purpose is to authorize that store.
